title: Rigveda 10.156: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.156: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.156 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 138r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.156.1-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 138r
translation.original_text:
1a̱gniṁ hi̍nvantu no̱ dhiya̱ḥ sapti̍m ā̱śum i̍vā̱jiṣu̍ | tena̍ jeṣma̱ dhana̍ṁ-dhanam ||
2yayā̱ gā ā̱karā̍mahe̱ sena̍yāgne̱ tavo̱tyā | tāṁ no̍ hinva ma̱ghatta̍ye ||
3āgne̍ sthū̱raṁ ra̱yim bha̍ra pṛ̱thuṁ goma̍ntam a̱śvina̍m | a̱ṅdhi khaṁ va̱rtayā̍ pa̱ṇim ||
4agne̱ nakṣa̍tram a̱jara̱m ā sūrya̍ṁ rohayo di̱vi | dadha̱j jyoti̱r jane̍bhyaḥ ||
5agne̍ ke̱tur vi̱śām a̍si̱ preṣṭha̱ḥ śreṣṭha̍ upastha̱sat | bodhā̍ sto̱tre vayo̱ dadha̍t ||
translation.text:
1LET songs of ours speed Agni forth like a fleet courser in the race, And we will win each prize through him.
2Agni the dart whereby we gain kine for ourselves with help from thee,– That send us for the gain of wealth.
3O Agni, bring us wealth secure, vast wealth in horses and in kine: Oil thou the socket, turn the wheel.
4O Agni, thou hast made the Sun, Eternal Star, to mount the sky, Bestowing light on living men.
5Thou, Agni, art the people's light, best, dearest, seated in thy shrine: Watch for the singer, give him life.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 138r (OPenn image 137, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.155.4 ‹-budbudayāśavaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 138v, begins in RV 10.157.2 ‹yajñaṁ ca nas tanvaṁ›. Verses 10.156.1-5 end on this page.
